content.comment_body: With [product_name] software version [version_no] installed on my computer, I've uploaded my program to a [product_name]. I want to remotely view several inputs for my small business. The business site uses a PLC-managed access system, which is connected via Ethernet to a PC and also links to the internet through a DSL router/modem. The [product_name] software isn't installed on the business PC. Do I need to connect the [product_name] to the site's Ethernet to use the Webserver monitoring feature, or can I connect it directly to a free port on the modem? The modem's IP address is 192.168.0.1 and I've set the [product_name]'s IP address to 192.168.0.60. What further configuration is needed for remote access from my computer or smartphone? I haven't found setup instructions in the manual and I have no networking experience.

Hello. I've tried using the web server feature. I connected my PLC to a Wi-Fi router, enabled the web server in the PLC settings, and found that to view I/O or control the PLC, I need to connect my phone to that router. By entering the PLC's IP address in the browser, you get a password prompt (which you can disable). If you have a static IP, it's best because you can access it remotely from anywhere.

Hi, how are you connecting the [product_name] to the internet—via DSL or a mobile network like 3G/LTE? If using DSL, setting up remote access is relatively straightforward. If using a mobile network, you'll need extra equipment (e.g., specific communication modules) to access your provider's network. For DSL: 1) Assign the [product_name]'s IP, enable Webserver and Remote Access; 2) Set up port forwarding on your DSL router (forward port 8080 to port 80 at the [product_name]'s IP); 3) Use DynDNS if you don't have a fixed IP for your router; 4) From your internet-connected PC or smartphone, enter the DynDNS address or IP of the [product_name] in your browser. Hope this helps.
Thanks, [user_name]. That's very useful. The site's modem is DSL. I'm looking into getting a static IP from my internet provider. They currently provide a static IP for payment processing.

Hi, have you enabled remote access for your [product_name] (via tools/transfer/access control)? Make sure to configure a password. On your DSL router, set up port forwarding from 8080 to the [product_name]'s IP address on port 80. Then try using the [product_name] web server. For security, using a VPN is recommended. Hope this helps.
This was very informative and helpful for everyone.
A new question placed by [user_name] has been moved to a different thread with the topic 'Can connect to [product_name] from internet via another location and network?' Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are searching for specific instructions to enable remote monitoring using the [product_name] web server. There is ongoing uncertainty and insufficient information in official manuals, particularly around networking setups involving Ethernet, DSL routers, and internet access. Users are asking for concrete configuration steps, such as port forwarding, IP setup, and security—especially VPN use. Many users lack networking background and need accessible guidance.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect simple, stepwise instructions that enable remote access to the [product_name] web server through a home or business DSL network. The goal is to allow monitoring from any Internet-connected device, even by those with limited networking knowledge.
